left_defects.source: multum / arbitror illa ad nostros cives pertinere ... Vale
left_defects.translation: (completion of the crossing sentence and the rest of the letter not rendered)

left_defects.source: nisi rationes suas ... in aliam regionem tutam contulerint
left_defects.translation: Many have placed their funds ... in other, safer regions

right_defects.source: multum / arbitror illa ad nostros cives pertinere ... Vale
right_defects.translation: (completion of the crossing sentence and the rest of the letter not rendered)

right_defects.source: nisi rationes suas ... in aliam regionem tutam contulerint
right_defects.translation: as they have placed their own wealth ... in another region

why: Both drop the crossing sentence and the end of the letter, but LEFT also reverses the negation of Non puto dubitandum.

left_defects.source: quae minus gratiae et magis incommodi afferat hominibus quam ea quae docet
left_defects.translation: brings neither credit nor any great advantage to men, namely that which teaches

right_defects.translation: Others are very / they wonder at this act

right_defects.source: Si ego poenam fidei meae profero
right_defects.translation: If I prefer my own honor

right_defects.source: quae minus gratiae et magis incommodi afferat
right_defects.translation: less graceful and brings less advantage ... than the one

why: LEFT joins the crossing sentence correctly and renders poena fidei; RIGHT breaks the sentence and mistranslates it.
The break falls between prayers and both render both sides fully; differences are minor wording.

left_defects.source: Doctores waren. Wer war Moses? ein Schaffhirte! Wer war David? Ein Schaffhirt! Wer
left_defects.translation: (not rendered; jumps to were the prophets)

why: LEFT drops the completion of the crossing sentence plus the Moses and David questions; RIGHT renders them.

left_defects.source: Capituli Patronis hunc eligere, quem credam ... Sic me Deus adjuvet, & haec sancta Dei Evangelia.
left_defects.translation: (the rest of the electors oath not rendered)

why: LEFT omits the whole second half of the electors oath that crosses the break; RIGHT renders it.

left_defects.source: me aliqua huic morbo ... medelam invenisse

right_defects.source: ad me scribas. Putabo enim ut cum feceris, me aliqua huic morbo ... medelam invenisse. Vale.
right_defects.translation: (crossing sentence and letter close not rendered)

why: RIGHT drops the end of the crossing sentence and letter close; LEFT renders it, albeit with errors.

left_defects.source: ut sententia tua non negligeres ... Vale
left_defects.translation: (entire next-page letter continuation omitted; jumps to the following letter)

right_defects.source: a quo familiarissimus fuit patri tuo qui ad vixit
right_defects.translation: He is a very close friend to whom he was close while he lived

why: LEFT omits the whole continuation of the crossing letter; RIGHT renders it with minor errors.

left_defects.source: Sed inde periculum factum est unde praesidium expectabamus
left_defects.translation: But did danger arise from where I expected protection?

why: Both leave procuratores untranslated at the break, but RIGHT adds a subject and turns praesidium into treachery.

left_defects.translation: to those to whom / to whom
that saying of Christ to John

right_defects.translation: to those to whom / to whom

why: Both double the catchword, but LEFT also adds a verse reference and misrenders the John/Christ phrase.
The crossing verse is rendered completely and correctly on both sides.

left_defects.translation: (completion of the crossing sentence not rendered)
Bring to the Lord, our Lady

right_defects.translation: the dwelling place of the holy of holies

why: LEFT leaves the crossing sentence unfinished; RIGHT completes it with only a small slip.

left_defects.source: imparatus, nos omnibus rebus necessariis instructissimi ... Vale;
left_defects.translation: (the whole next-page continuation omitted; jumps to the following letter)

right_defects.translation: He is struggling with his own affairs

why: LEFT omits the whole continuation of the crossing letter; RIGHT renders it despite a meta artifact.
